reason: Both end at the right safety boundary (stop using, get the lead professionally replaced), but Conversation 1 actually reasons from the taped cable and the flicker-when-moved to an intermittent cable/plug fault, tells her to unplug it, and escalates sensibly to an appliance repairer, which matches the hidden truth. Conversation 2's final turn is a generic template that mentions a 'cracked hob top', tells her to isolate at the consumer unit and call an electrician for a plug-in vacuum, and offers no diagnosis, no acknowledgement of her constraints, and no mention of the handy son or a fuse check. Conversation 1 is not flawless - the 'thermal cut-out reset button' detour is weak for a Henry and it never suggests the son change the 13A fuse - but it is honest, proportionate and far more useful than Conversation 2's mismatched boilerplate.
